# SOP-P1-L4-01 Line startup - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
Related: SB-1046, SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04

1. Purpose and scope  
   1.1 Purpose: Provide the controlled procedure to start up the Heat Treat line for production runs, ensuring equipment readiness, process safety, and traceable records.  
   1.2 Scope: Applies to operators, maintenance, and quality personnel working on EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03.

2. Background and rationale  
   The Heat Treat line integrates CNC pre-machining, hydraulic press operations, and a batch furnace. Proper startup sequences prevent part damage, preserve process capability, and reduce safety risks. The spindle warm-up sequence and controlled furnace quench timing are critical to dimensional stability and metallurgical outcome. Examples: insufficient spindle warm-up increases runout and causes scrap; excessive quench delay in the furnace degrades hardness and results in rework.

3. Preconditions (must be verified before proceeding)  
   3.1 Facility utilities are online and stable per SB-1046.  
   3.2 Last shift maintenance work has been completed and closed in the maintenance system referenced in SOP-P1-L4-03.  
   3.3 All protection interlocks are present and functional; isolation permits removed.  
   3.4 Production plan and heat numbers available and matched to carrier trays as required by SOP-P1-L4-04.

4. Required PPE  
   - Safety glasses with side shields  
   - Heat-resistant gloves when loading/unloading EQ-P1-L4-HT03 per furnace access procedure  
   - Hearing protection while near operating EQ-P1-L4-HP02 during press cycles  
   - High-visibility clothing for shop floor access

5. Startup procedure (numbered steps)  
   5.1 Visual inspection  
       5.1.1 Confirm work area clear of obstructions and loose tooling.  
       5.1.2 Verify emergency stops are accessible and labeled. Rationale: removes mechanical hazards and ensures operator response capability. Example: remove pneumatic hoses left on the floor that can entangle operators or tooling.  
   5.2 Power-up sequence  
       5.2.1 Enable main feed to EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and EQ-P1-L4-HT03 following lockout/tagout verification. Rationale: proper sequenced energization prevents inrush events and alarm floods.  
   5.3 CNC warm-up and verification for EQ-P1-L4-CN01  
       5.3.1 Home axes and confirm position feedback within acceptable limits.  
       5.3.2 Execute spindle warm-up as documented on the operator screen. The spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes. Rationale: thermal stabilization reduces spindle runout and improves first-piece accuracy. Example: when warming from a cold start, run a lightweight program with tool touches to confirm consistent surface finish. Record: spindle warm-up start and stop timestamps in the log.  
   5.4 Hydraulic press readiness for EQ-P1-L4-HP02  
       5.4.1 Verify hydraulic reservoir level and filter condition per maintenance checklist. Rationale: low fluid or clogged filters can change force characteristics. Record: hydraulic checklist signed and filed.  
       5.4.2 Run a no-load cycle to confirm valve sequencing and pressure rise within control band. Rationale: confirms safe actuation prior to loading production pieces.  
   5.5 Furnace startup and control verification for EQ-P1-L4-HT03  
       5.5.1 Validate furnace control communication and that thermocouples report expected steady-state values per operator display. Rationale: ensures accurate soak and ramp control before loading parts.  
       5.5.2 Confirm automatic quench system primed and ready. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 15 seconds. Rationale: constraining quench delay preserves metallurgical properties and meets hardness targets. Example: when cycling a dummy load, monitor the quench activation time from furnace door close to quench onset and log the measured delay. Record: quench delay verification entry in the process validation log.  
   5.6 First-piece flow test  
       5.6.1 Process a single carrier through EQ-P1-L4-CN01 → EQ-P1-L4-HP02 → EQ-P1-L4-HT03 following the normal material flow. Observe for mechanical interference, tool breakage, or abnormal temperatures. Rationale: verifies integrated flow before committing full lot. Record: first-piece inspection checklist including dimensional and visual acceptance criteria.

6. Process monitoring and records to keep  
   - Spindle warm-up log for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 (start/stop times).  
   - Hydraulic readiness checklist for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 (filter status, fluid level, no-load cycle result).  
   - Furnace control verification and quench delay verification for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 with timestamped readings.  
   - First-piece inspection checklist and material traceability tags.  
   - Any deviations or alarms recorded in the line event log and routed to quality per SOP-P1-L4-03.

7. Abnormal conditions and escalation  
   7.1 If spindle parameters do not stabilize after the warm-up period, stop the line and notify maintenance. Rationale: continued operation risks scrap and tool damage.  
   7.2 If measured quench delay exceeds the maximum referenced value, halt loading into the furnace and follow the stoppage criteria in SOP-P1-L4-04. Rationale: prevents out-of-spec metallurgical results.  
   7.3 For any hydraulic pressure abnormality, depressurize and tag out EQ-P1-L4-HP02 until inspected by maintenance.

8. Training and competency  
   Operators must be trained on the startup checklist, emergency stop actions, and use of the records system. Training completion is documented per site training policy and referenced in SB-1046.

9. Sign-off and acceptance  
   9.1 Operator initiating startup signs and dates the startup checklist and attaches all required logs.  
   9.2 Quality representative verifies first-piece acceptance and initials the checklist to allow full production release.  
   9.3 Maintenance representative signs off when any equipment actions were performed during startup.

10. Revision history and attachments  
   See related documents SB-1046, SOP-P1-L4-03, SOP-P1-L4-04 for linked procedures, maintenance forms, and detailed quality criteria.

Signatures:  
Operator: ____________________  
Quality: ____________________  
Maintenance: ____________________
